decision: accept exact Latin source/body merits and proposed finite tuples on a qualified basis; Root adoption and code/runtime admission remain pending
source_fidelity: The selected complete Latin petition matches the inspected secondary comparison in lexical content and word order under the declared accent, ligature, capitalization, pointing and line-break treatment. Its complete short conclusion and distinct response are independently sourced, not falsely attributed as fully printed in the old petition or abbreviated comparison cue.
conclusion_and_response: The complete formula Per Christum Dominum nostrum and separately marked Amen were directly read in the Latin column of Lasance printed217, retained derivative page1. The response glyph is explicitly normalized to R. on a separate line. Secondary digital2002 IGMR77/AP22 governs the three offerings; IGMR89/AP24 governs the three Postcommunions. Each actual receiving prayer prints the Through-Christ cue, addresses the Father in its complete context, and has no final Son reference requiring another branch. The Body-and-Blood words near the opening of OT12 Postcommunion do not make its ending a final Son reference or a direct address to the Son.
surface_assessment: The same qualified underlying-expression basis is proposed separately for web, download, print, cli, corpus-data and public-git. No surface permission is inferred from an ICEL web grant or from English acceptance. Only the exact named study carrier and notice are covered; protected comparator pages, their whole delivery, modern apparatus, other prayers and liturgical authorization are excluded.
grade_assessment: The consumer relationship is source-based-latin-study-reconstruction. Carrier equality does not establish identity to an old book or authenticated modern target. Medium grades in the offerings/OT11 and high source-provenance confidence in OT8/12 are bounded by their stated collation to the declared carrier; this review’s legal-merits confidence remains moderate for all six. Authenticated printed2002 fidelity and complete2008 correspondence remain unestablished.
independence: Fresh direct inspection and Latin-specific whole-expression reasoning; earlier independent English/source merits are corroborating evidence only. No contemporary approved English was used as Latin authority. No new acquisition, canonical mutation or production runtime test was performed.
limitations: No exact older whole revised reading is established; no exhaustive new negative-source search is claimed. Specific protected new authorship or a material source/body/tuple mismatch would require reassessment. Any changed owner, body, payload, proof, source, notice, grade or surface is outside this exact recommendation.
source_finding: Feltoe1896 AP92/p68, XX Item alia: complete two-line Hostias offering prayer before the Preface. Marked Domine and sanctificando contractions are expanded; the literal per cue is preserved separately. Wilson1915 AP236/p178 is a separately read complete parallel with a different sanctification construction; it is not silently corrected or combined with Feltoe.
receiving_context: Secondary digital2002 AP270 explicitly heads Ordinary TimeIII and contains the complete offering petition with its Through-Christ cue.
exact_change_assessment: The sacrificial-offerings noun becomes gifts explicitly belonging to us; the offered modifier is deleted; the relative pronoun and result adjective take the required neuter forms; the direct make-salutary request is recast as grant-that-they-will-be-salutary. The actor sanctifying, beneficiaries and ordered reception/sanctification/salvation relationship are preserved.
affirmative_whole_expression: I independently find a defensible nonoriginal-adaptation basis for this entire Latin unit. Feltoe already supplies the complete linked expression: placated reception of the offered things, their divine sanctification, and their saving result for the petitioners. The revised possessive makes the offering relation explicit; the new gift designation and grant/result construction are conventional ways of stating that same dependent request. Taken together, they do not organize a new sequence of petitions or introduce an independently developed image. The complete old short conclusion and marked response are conventional completion of that same prayer, not a new expressive composition assembled from scattered substantive clauses.
strongest_contrary: The possessive and changed grant construction are genuine lexical and syntactic choices, and the result clause has a different cadence and more explicit prospective form. A court could find original editorial expression even where the theological request stays the same. The old source does not contain the exact resulting wording. My qualified affirmative depends on the conventional function of this particular aggregate recast within the continuous old prayer, not its short length or an assumption that synonyms are always free.
individual_disposition: Qualified affirmative, moderate confidence. Neither the distinctive alternative Hadrianum syntax nor fragments from it are needed to manufacture an exact old match.
